sections.h2: Where is Chili, NY, and what kind of town is it?
sections.html:
Chili is a suburban town in the southwest corner of Monroe County, and its northeastern corner touches the city of Rochester. The town was cut from Riga on February 22, 1822, and it covers about 39.9 square miles, almost all of it land. Downtown Rochester sits roughly 7 miles northeast of the hamlet of Chili Center.

Both Interstate 490 and the New York State Thruway cross the town. The town's own communities include Chili Center, North Chili (home to Roberts Wesleyan University), South Chili along the Thruway, West Chili near Black Creek Park, and the rural hamlet of Clifton. Black Creek Park runs nature trails along the creek, and the Genesee River forms part of the eastern edge.

sections.h2: Which school districts and roads matter when you list a Chili house?
sections.html:
Chili is split among several districts, so the district for your address depends on which part of town you live in. The Churchville-Chili, Gates Chili and Wheatland-Chili central school districts all serve the town, and the town's own assessment paperwork also lists Caledonia-Mumford as a district that can apply to a parcel in Chili. Check the school line on your tax bill before you quote a district to a buyer.

The town's road signs read like a local map. State Route 33A is Chili Avenue, State Route 386 is the Scottsville-Chili Road, and State Route 252 is Beaver Road. Town Hall is at 3333 Chili Avenue, which is also where the Assessor and the Building Department work.

  • Commuters reach Rochester on I-490 or Chili Avenue.
  • The Thruway gives a direct east-west route through South Chili.
  • Buyers who work at Roberts Wesleyan or in the North Chili area often look at the northwest side of town first.

sections.h2: How does Chili assess a house, and how do I challenge the number?
sections.html:
Chili says every property in town is assessed at 100 percent of market value, using a July 1, 2024 valuation date for the current roll. For the 2026 roll the valuation date was July 1, 2025. The Assessor sets value and runs exemptions, while the school boards, the County Legislature and the Town Board set the tax rates.

The yearly cycle is simple. March 1 is the taxable status date and the exemption deadline. The tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day falls on the fourth Tuesday in May, and the final roll is filed July 1. The 2026 Board of Assessment Review met on Tuesday, May 26, so that date has passed, and the next one comes in May 2027.

There are three levels of review, and each one wants evidence.

  • An informal review with the Assessor, by appointment from October through March, may include an inside and outside inspection.
  • A formal grievance goes to the five-resident Board of Assessment Review on form RP-524. The signed original must arrive with five copies, and faxed or emailed applications are not accepted.
  • If the board's decision disappoints you, a small claims assessment review petition (RPTL-730) is filed with the Monroe County Clerk within 30 days of the final roll, for a $30 fee.

Useful evidence includes a recent appraisal, a purchase contract, comparable sales, and photographs of deferred maintenance. If you plan to sell, a signed listing or purchase offer is also the kind of document the board asks to see.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Chili, and what happens to the bill when I sell?
sections.html:
The Town of Chili Receiver of Taxes collects the town and county bill, and the school districts bill separately. Town and county bills are mailed at the very end of December and should arrive by the end of the first week of January. School bills go out at the very end of August and should arrive by the end of the first week of September. Homeowners with an escrow account get a receipt rather than a bill.

Paying by card at the Chili tax counter or on the town website carries a processing fee. Debit cards have a $3.95 minimum, and credit cards cost 2.45 percent with the same $3.95 minimum. Payments owed to the County Treasurer for delinquent taxes go through the Monroe County website, so check which office the bill names before you pay.

After a sale, the old bill belongs to the new owner. The town asks the seller either to return the bill to the Receiver with the new owner's name or to forward it directly. A new owner may also face an exemption recapture charge, which the Assessor sets as a one-time amount when the previous owner had an exemption the buyer does not qualify for. If you carried Senior, Veterans or Disability exemptions, tell your buyer before closing so the charge is not a surprise.

sections.h2: What does the Chili Building Department look at before a sale?
sections.html:
The Building Department enforces the Chili town code and the New York building codes, and it issues certificates of occupancy or compliance after a final inspection. A project with a permit is not finished until that certificate is issued. Permit applications go through the CloudPermit online system, and the department answers questions about zoning and planning approvals.

These local rules come up most often in resale conversations.

  • Sheds from 1 to 119 square feet need no permit, sheds from 120 to 196 square feet need a building permit, and sheds of 197 square feet or more need a permit and a variance.
  • Fences need no permit unless the lot is in a flood zone or the fence sits in an easement.
  • Upgrading an electrical panel requires a building permit.
  • Domesticated farm animals, including chickens, need at least 5 acres.
  • The code enforcement officer responds to complaints about rubbish, litter, tall grass and unlicensed vehicles that can be seen from the public right of way.

An instrument survey map is often requested at closing. Look through your own closing papers first, then ask the Building Department whether one is on file. The Monroe County Clerk is the next place to check.

sections.h2: What happens at the Monroe County Clerk when a Chili deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Every Chili sale is recorded at the Monroe County Clerk's Office, 39 W. Main Street in downtown Rochester. The county lists a one-page deed at $50 with $5 for each added page. Filing the TP-584 transfer tax return costs $5, the RP-5217 equalization form costs $125 for residential property (and $250 for other property), and each residential deed carries another $10 fee.

Transfer tax at this office is $4 per thousand dollars of price. That matches the state rate of $2 for each $500, which the seller pays, and it is due with the TP-584 within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The state also adds a 1 percent charge on residences sold for $1 million or more, paid by the buyer.

The deed must be a dated original with grantor and grantee addresses, a legal description naming the municipality, the new tax number, original signatures and a notary acknowledgment. To record the same day, you must be in line by 4:30. A buyer who purchases for cash and as-is still goes through this same recording step, so your closing timeline depends on how complete your paperwork is, not on the buyer's financing.

faqs.q: What is the population of Chili, NY?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 29,123 people in the town of Chili, up 1.7 percent from 28,625 in 2010. Chili is a Monroe County suburb of Rochester.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Chili?
faqs.a: It falls on the fourth Tuesday in May each year. In 2026 the board met on May 26, and the 2027 date will be the fourth Tuesday of that May, so file form RP-524 with supporting evidence by 8 pm that day.

faqs.q: Which office collects property tax for a Chili house?
faqs.a: The Chili Receiver of Taxes collects the town and county bill at Town Hall, 3333 Chili Avenue. Delinquent taxes go to the Monroe County Treasury, and the school districts send their own bills in September.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Chili house?
faqs.a: The town issues a certificate of occupancy or compliance when permitted work passes its final inspection. If you did work without a permit, ask the Building Department what is required to close it out before you list.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Monroe County?
faqs.a: A one-page deed is $50 plus $5 per extra page, with $5 for the TP-584, $125 for the RP-5217 on residential property, a $10 residential deed fee, and transfer tax of $4 per thousand dollars of price.
